subject: Post-call: Model fit & eval follow-up — PayGrid / acceptance thresholds
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@paygrid.com>; Rajesh Kumar <rajesh.k@paygrid.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com; dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Model fit & eval follow-up — PayGrid / acceptance thresholds

Hi Samantha / Rajesh —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery:

- Goal: Improve behavioral classification and routing accuracy for payments support flows while keeping latency under 120ms P95.
- Current baseline: PayGrid internal fine-tuned model (PT-Baseline v3) — you reported ~86% macro-F1 on the sample set and median latency ~90ms on your infra.
- Our recommendation: start with two open variants for parity testing — Llama-2-13B-chat (quantized) and Mistral-Instruct-7B — plus Redwood-verified compiled variants (int8-friendly runtimes).
- Acceptance thresholds (proposal): match or exceed +1.5% absolute on macro-F1 versus PT-Baseline on your key prompt set OR no more than 1% relative drop if we can demonstrate 30-40% unit-cost savings and meet latency SLO.

Attachments: paygrid_eval_report_20260323.pdf (high-level summary), prompt_set_paygrid_v1.jsonl (your prompt set, sanitized), benchmark_results_paygrid_20260324.csv (initial microbenchmarks we ran on similar workloads).

Next steps I propose:
1) Redwood runs the prompt_set_paygrid_v1.jsonl against the three candidate variants and returns a side-by-side results table + qualitative failure cases (3-5 mins per prompt). Target: results in 48 hours.
2) If a variant meets acceptance thresholds, scope a 2-week pilot with limited traffic routing and production telemetry.
3) Technical sync: aditya/deep-dive on quantization/latency tradeoffs (30 mins) — how does quantization affect your edge-case pass rates?

Can you confirm the acceptance thresholds above (match+1.5% or <=1% drop with cost/latency benefit) and that we should go ahead with the 48-hour run?

Thanks,

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

From: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh.k@paygrid.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>; Samantha Lee <samantha@paygrid.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com; dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & eval follow-up — PayGrid / acceptance thresholds

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side before you run the 48-hour pass: 

- Acceptance: The match+1.5% threshold is sensible. For the cost/latency conditional acceptance, we want to limit overall user-facing regression to <=0.5% on any single critical intent (we have 4 critical intents). Does Redwood have a way to guarantee per-intent bounds or at least flag regressions at that granularity?
- Regression concerns: Our baseline was tuned on internal proprietary data; open models sometimes hit parity on average but miss edge cases (billing dispute language, microflow contexts). Can you include a failure-case summary that highlights which intents/regimes the model regresses on?
- Latency & throughput: 120ms P95 is our target; ideally <100ms P95. How much does int8 quantization vs int4 affect the observed pass rates in your experience?
- Data handling: For the 48-hour run, we need assurances around retention and that test logs won't be used to further train public models.

If you can address these, please proceed. Also loop in your security/contact for the data handling note.

— Rajesh
Rajesh Kumar
Director, ML Platform | PayGrid
rajesh.k@paygrid.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh.k@paygrid.com>; Samantha Lee <samantha@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>; dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & eval follow-up — PayGrid / acceptance thresholds

Hi Rajesh / Samantha —

Quick technical notes to address the asks: 

1) Per-intent regression detection: we'll run the supplied prompt set with intent labels (as in prompt_set_paygrid_v1.jsonl). Our eval harness produces per-intent confusion matrices and will flag any intent with >0.5% absolute drop. We'll include a per-intent dashboard link in the results.

2) Failure-case summaries: we'll output the top 25 failed prompts per variant with short annotations (token-level diffs + likely cause: context truncation / hallucination / instruction following). That will make edge-case regressions visible.

3) Quantization tradeoffs: based on our compiled-runtime experiments:
   - int8 (dynamic quant) on Llama-2-13B-chat: typical macro-F1 delta vs fp16 is ~0.8-1.5% depending on prompt length; P95 latency improvement ~30-40% on A100/80GB-class hosts.
   - int4 aggressive quant: cost/latency wins up to 55-60% but can incur 2-4% macro-F1 drop on instruction-heavy, long-context prompts.
   - Mistral-Instruct-7B tends to be robust int8 with <1% delta and very favorable latency/cost profile for short prompts.

4) Data handling: Redwood will run the eval in a private test harness scoped to the PayGrid pilot (no retention beyond 30 days, logs restricted to the PayGrid project, and not used to further train public models). I'll loop in our security contact for the formal DPA/processing note if needed.

Proposed timeline: run the candidate variants against prompt_set_paygrid_v1.jsonl by end of day Thu (48 hours). I’ll attach the initial benchmark CSV we ran on similar workloads (benchmark_results_paygrid_20260324.csv) and a short eval report.

If that works, we'll share the results + a short Miro with failure cases and per-intent charts.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Systems Engineer, Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

Marissa / Aditya —

This looks good. We confirm:
- Acceptance thresholds: match+1.5% or <=1% aggregate drop with >30% cost savings, AND no single critical intent dropping >0.5% absolute.
- Please proceed with the 48-hour run. We'll provide any missing intent labels by EOD.
- Data handling: Rajesh flagged retention — we need the DPA note. Please include security contact in the next thread.

For logistics: can you also provide a short mutual action plan (owner + due date) so we can track in our internal tracker? If possible, schedule the 30-min technical sync for Thu 9:00 AM PT.

Thanks — looking forward to results.

— Samantha
